title: Velocity magnitude at impact
description: Essential: The final numerical answer for the speed of sphere a when b hits the ground must be 5 m/s.

title: Maximum height reached
description: Essential: The final numerical answer for the maximum height of sphere a must be 3.75 m.

title: Work-energy theorem application
description: Important: The solution must apply the work-energy theorem to the two-sphere system to relate the change in gravitational potential energy to the gain in kinetic energy.

title: Post-impact motion analysis
description: Important: After sphere b hits the ground, the solution must analyze sphere a's motion as a projectile or under gravity alone to find its additional rise.

title: Correct mass consideration
description: Important: The kinetic energy term must correctly use the sum of the masses (m_a + m_b) since both spheres move with the same speed while connected.

title: Total height calculation
description: Optional: The final maximum height should be correctly found by adding the initial height h to the additional height h' gained after the impact.

title: Sign error in energy
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly assigning signs to the change in potential energy for each mass (e.g., m_a*g*h should be positive if h is its rise).

title: Ignoring post-impact motion
description: Pitfall: Assuming sphere a stops when sphere b hits the ground, and not calculating its continued upward motion.
